newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin considers Europe for Clinton summit - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin considers Europe for Clinton summit - Tass.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is considering the possibility of having a planned summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton next month shifted from Washington to Europe, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Friday.

The agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying a change of venue to Europe was one of several possibilities Yeltsin was weighing. It was the first time the Kremlin had said officially that Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, was considering any such change.
Yastrzhembsky, in comments that clearly put the onus for any revision on Washington, said Yeltsin would listen to arguments put by Clinton before making any final decision.
He would also consult Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin who is expected to meet Clinton in Washington on Friday. Final arrangements would be made by telephone or an exchange of envoys.

No firm date has been set yet for the summit and Yeltsin's poor health has given rise to speculation that he might be reluctant to make the long journey to Washington. He cancelled a visit to the Netherlands earlier this month and is under doctors' orders to limit his workload.
The Kremlin said Yeltsin would meet his chief aide Anatoly Chubais on Friday at his Gorky-9 country residence.

Yeltsin was shown on television on Thursday addressing the nation directly for the first time since his release from hospital on January 20. He spoke for less than a minute, vowing that proposals to limit pension payments would not be implemented.
His voice was steady, his speech slow and his manner determined, but he had clearly aged considerably since a quintuple heart bypass operation in November.
